day.text: Emu here, visited Alex, nothing happened, no eggs gained. Drew's story is odd: Pigeon lays eggs in others, so who laid one in you? Drew looks shady to me.
day.note: Alex is my Meowfia teammate; steer suspicion to Drew, whose claim is odd.

day.text: Casey, Farm. I visited Drew and my nest didn't change. Blair's 5 matches my 5 cards, so I believe Lyrebird. Drew's +1 fits my visit too. Alex and Ellis, what are your claims?
day.note: Blair's claim fits my 5 eggs. Drew's egg matches my visit.

day.text: Alex, Pigeon, visited Casey, no change for me. Casey never named a role, which is suspicious. Drew and Casey both say they visited each other's side, so one of them is covering. I'm leaning Casey.
day.note: I know Casey is Farm Pigeon, so Drew's claim is false and Drew is probably Meowfia. To win I need a Farm player eggsecuted, so I'll cast doubt on Casey.

day.text: Casey, you said Farm but not your animal. Name it. Drew, you and Casey can't both be Pigeon.
Correction, I'm Pigeon visiting Casey, sorry, mixed up. Casey still never named a role, and Alex says they visited Casey with no change, which a Pigeon would have caused. I'm with Alex: Casey.
day.note: Rally against Casey, who is surely Farm.

day.text: I'm the Emu, I was dealt it. Ellis, you're lying. Nobody laid an egg in me, so Alex and Drew, your claims that you visited me as Pigeon are false. Drew also changed his story. Blair is the only one whose numbers check out. I'm throwing at Drew.
day.note: I'm the real Emu; Ellis's claim is false. Alex and Drew claims contradict my 0 eggs.

day.text: Math check: Alex and Drew both claim they visited Casey as Pigeon, yet Casey's nest is unchanged at 5. Both can't be true, and Drew already flipped his story. I'm throwing at Drew; Alex is my second suspect.
day.note: Alex and Drew both claim Pigeon visiting Casey, but Casey unchanged; both lying.

day.text: Fine, I'll concede on Emu being Casey's if it's real. Drew changed his story, that's the weakest link. Throwing at Drew.
day.note: Go with majority on Drew; avoid Alex.
Consensus on Drew; end the day.
Silent this beat; will throw one low card at Casey later.

review.headline: Three cats outnumber the farm, then two of them egg their own teammate.
review.summary: Wolfsbane made three of five players Meowfia, and all three were House Cats. They had the voting majority and still lost. Drew gave a sloppy Pigeon claim, changed it, and the whole table piled on him, including fellow cat Ellis. Blair's Lyrebird turned one free visit into 5 extra cards, and those cards became the biggest throw and the winning score.

rounds.recap: Blair claimed Lyrebird and got +5, which matched Casey's 5-card nest. Casey correctly claimed Emu and confirmed Drew's +1. Drew first said he visited Blair as Pigeon, then switched to Casey, whose nest never changed. That made him the obvious target. Blair, Casey and cat Ellis threw 14 cards at Drew, and Drew was eggsecuted as Meowfia.

highlights.text: Casey's line 'Alex and Drew, your claims that you visited me as Pigeon are false' used one unchanged nest to expose two liars.
Drew went from 'visited Blair' to 'visited Casey' within one beat. That flip decided the round.
Ellis knew Alex was a House Cat, so a fellow cat, and still threw four 10+ cards at fellow cat Drew. Ellis lost all of them and finished on 1 point.
Alex and Drew each threw one card at Farm Casey and got it back as consolation. It was the only good bet the cats made.

confusions.what: Ellis acted like a Farm player at the vote and threw 43 points of high cards at Drew. Ellis was Meowfia, and the only cat in the pool was the House Cat, so Drew had to be a teammate. Throwing at your own team gives no consolation.

Drew's first claim was 'Pigeon, visited Blair, got 1 egg myself.' That doesn't fit Pigeon at all, since Pigeons lay eggs in other nests. He then changed his visit to Casey, even though he already knew Casey's nest was unchanged.
Alex knew Casey was the Pigeon, yet claimed to be a Pigeon who visited Casey. Casey's nest had not changed, so the claim could be checked and shown false at once.
In the survey Ellis put Drew at only 50% Meowfia. Ellis did not realise that with only the House Cat in the pool, every Meowfia is a House Cat.
Blair said the 5 eggs were 'capped'. Casey's nest held exactly 5, so the cap never applied. This is minor.

design_notes: Wolfsbane with only the House Cat in the pool means every Meowfia is a House Cat. Any cat that investigates another cat learns it has found a teammate, which breaks 'Meowfia don't know each other.' Consider adding a second cat to the pool, or blocking Wolfsbane until the pool has more cats.

The Lyrebird is too strong at the start. Every nest starts at 5 or more, so visiting anyone gives the full +5. That doubled Blair's votes and banked 33 points. Try counting only eggs gained that night, or capping the Lyrebird at 2 or 3.

Three cats held 16 of the 26 votes and still lost because they can't coordinate. With Wolfsbane, a cat majority is common. Without some coordination tool, a Meowfia majority mostly produces cats throwing at each other.

In a one-round game, losing on your own team costs everything thrown. Ellis lost 43 points and Blair won by 33. A single misread vote decides the whole game. Consider playing more rounds, or giving a small floor for losers.

The Emu worked well as a truthful claim that sounded strange. The fallback to Pigeon still let Casey's egg evidence clear Drew's +1. Also, the log prints the 'Nest sizes' line twice at the start of the day. That looks like an app bug.
review.title: Cats Egg Their Own
